name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type II

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Palmini Classification for Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells on histopathological examination
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening, blurring of the gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign
Focal epilepsy refractory to medical treatment with seizure onset consistent with lesion location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of dysmorphic neurons and/or balloon cells with supportive MRI findings and clinical presentation of focal refractory epilepsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation; MRI findings may be subtle and require high-resolution imaging.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal epileptic seizures with impaired awareness
Focal cortical thickening with transmantle sign on MRI
searchTerms: brain scan shows thick cortex with transmantle sign
MRI finding of cortical thickening and transmantle
focal cortical thickening with specific MRI sign

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to seizure burden
searchTerms: memory and learning issues related to seizures
head pain during or after seizures
mild weakness on opposite side of brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Developmental delay in early onset cases
Psychiatric comorbidities including depression and anxiety
searchTerms: mental health issues including anxiety and depression

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign
High-resolution 3T MRI preferred for lesion detection
genetic: Somatic mutations in MTOR pathway genes in some cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement with skin, renal, and cardiac lesions
Presence of cortical tubers rather than isolated focal dysplasia
Genetic mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes
Presence of a benign tumor on imaging
Typically associated with seizures but distinct lesion morphology

redFlags: New onset focal seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
Progressive neurological deficits contralateral to lesion
references: Palmini A, et al. Focal cortical dysplasias: neuropathological subtypes and surgical outcome. Brain. 2004.
Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification. Epilepsia. 2011.
Wang Y, et al. Somatic mutations in MTOR cause focal cortical dysplasia type II. Nat Genet. 2016.
